{{Quote|Cho mai translates as "to cut off the weapon hand." Because this strike instantly ends an opponent's ability to use a weapon but does not kill, cho mai is always a preferred move in combat.|[[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]]|<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
In [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]], '''''cho mai''''' was the act of [[Dismemberment/Legends|cutting off]] an opponent's weapon hand.

==Application and description==
[[File:RikkarSlash.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Darth Kruhl]] uses ''cho mai'' against [[Rikkar-Du]].]]
''Cho mai'' was a precision technique as it demonstrated the skill of a swordsman. Considered honorable among [[Light side of the Force/Legends|lightsiders]], it allowed for a victory by causing minimal physical damage. [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Darksiders]] consider the mark to be merciful as such individuals prefer to [[Death/Legends|kill]] opponents rather than maim.<ref name="JvS" />

In lightsaber combat, ''cho mai'' was often performed by simply driving the opponents blade aside before cutting at the wrist.<ref name="SWTESB" /> Other methods include altering the angle of one's parry to catch the opponent's wrist instead of the blade or sliding the weapon inside an opponent's guard during a bladelock to cut off their hand. An even more vicious method consisted of grabbing the opponent's wrist and holding it in place while cutting it off.<ref name="SWROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Executing ''cho mai'' was often a question of recognizing an opening and exploiting it, attacking when the opponent left their weapon hand vulnerable. [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] commonly used it against [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]]-wielding opponents.

==Notable examples==
In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], in their [[Skirmish over Phaegon III|first duel]], [[Saes Rrogon]] used ''cho mai'' on [[Relin Druur]].<ref name="Crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref>

In [[3951 BBY]], aboard the [[Hammerhead-class cruiser|''Hammerhead''-class cruiser]], [[Harbinger (Hammerhead-class)|''Harbinger'']], [[Darth Sion]] initiated ''cho mai'' against [[Kreia]]. During the [[Battle of Malachor|confrontation]] between [[Meetra Surik]] and Darth Traya, the former used ''cho mai'' against her after weakening the Sith Lord.<ref name="KOTOR II">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

In [[990 BBY]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] applied ''cho mai'' on [[Hetton]] shortly before [[Duel on Ambria (990 BBY)|finishing him off]] on [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]]. Shortly afterwords, he severed the weapon hand of [[Johun Othone]] while they [[Duel on Tython|dueled]] in [[Belia Darzu]]'s stronghold.<ref name="DBROT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref>

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] used ''cho mai'' against the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] when she tried to shoot him in the back in the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]]. Days later, [[Mace Windu]] would employ the technique to bisect [[Jango Fett]]'s [[WESTAR-35 blaster pistol|blaster]] and then decapitated the Mandalorian. [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] also used ''cho mai'' against [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] in a duel during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle Of Geonosis]].<ref name="ATOC">{{Film|II}}</ref>

In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker used ''cho mai'' against [[TV-94/Legends|Tactical Droid TV-94]] when he tortured [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]] and during the [[Battle of Saleucami/Legends|First Battle of Saleucami]].<ref name="Grievous Intrigue">{{TCW|Grievous Intrigue}}</ref> In that same year, he later used ''cho mai'' against bounty hunter [[Twazzi/Legends|Twazzi]] when she tried to punch him.<ref name="Crises on Naboo">{{TCW|Crisis on Naboo}}</ref>

In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] used ''cho mai'' against [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] in the [[Battle of Dathomir/Legends|Battle of Dathomir]]. She severed one of the general's arms off in an attempt to defeat him, but failed.<ref name="Massacre">{{TCW|Massacre}}</ref>

Later on, [[Nightbrothers/Legends|Nightbrother]] [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]] [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] used ''cho mai'' against [[Tatsu]] when he called him a coward in a duel.<ref name="Sith Brothers">''[[The Clone Wars: The Sith Hunters]]''</ref> Shortly after, Obi-Wan Kenobi used ''cho mai'' against Savage during the [[Skirmish on Florrum/Legends|Skirmish on Florrum]].<ref name="Revival">{{TCW|Revival (episode)}}</ref>

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Anakin Skywalker used ''cho mai'' on Dooku shortly before killing him through ''[[Sai cha/Legends|Sai cha]]'' on the Separatist flagship [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']] with [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]'s encouragement.<ref name="SWROTS" />

During the [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|Battle of Utapau]], Obi-Wan used ''cho mai'' twice against General Grievous.<ref name="SWROTS" />

Near the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Skywalker again applied ''cho mai'' on [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], leading to his death at the hands of Skywalker's soon-to-be [[Sith Master/Legends|master]]. Prior to this incident, Grand Master Yoda used this technique against a clone trooper of the 501st Legion when he and Obi-Wan Kenobi engaged these clones outside the Jedi Temple.<ref name="SWROTS" />

In 19 BBY, Darth Vader assailed a [[Conclave on Kessel|secret meeting of surviving Jedi]] with the first to die by his blade being the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Sia-Lan Wezz]], having been [[Shiak|impaled]] by the Dark Lord before cutting of her hand as she fell dead, adding insult to injury.<ref name="Star Wars: Purge">[[Purge (comic book)|''Purge'']]</ref> That same year, Vader utilized ''cho mai'' in combination with a [[Telekinesis/Legends|lightsaber throw]] to sever the hand of [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Kai Hudorra]] during the failed [[ambush at Kestavel]].<ref name="DT32">[[Dark Times—A Spark Remains 5|''Dark Times—A Spark Remains'' 5]]</ref>

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Obi-Wan used ''cho mai'' in Mos Eisley cantina to protect Luke Skywalker from [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]] and [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]]. Baba lost half his arm during this engagement.<ref name="ANH" />

[[File:Cho_Mai_Jung_Ma.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A ''cho mai'' maneuver combined with [[Jung ma]].]]
In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Luke Skywalker bisected a wampa's arm when the creature threatened to eat him on Hoth. Darth Vader later severed Skywalker's right hand during the [[Duel on Cloud City/Legends|duel]] at [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].<ref name="SWTESB" /> 

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Luke Skywalker returned the favor during his rematch with Vader during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].<ref name="SWROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

In [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], during a brief but fierce duel, Luke Skywalker proved victorious after cutting off the hand of a [[Essence transfer|reborn]] Palpatine during the [[Battle of Pinnacle Base]].<ref name="Dark Empire">[[Dark Empire 6|''Dark Empire'' 6]]</ref>

[[Jaden Korr]], like his former master [[Kyle Katarn]], was quite skilled in applying ''cho mai'' just after winning bladelocks.<ref name="Jedi Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref><ref name="Jedi Outcast">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref>

Years later, [[Lumiya]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lady of the Sith]], used this technique on Luke Skywalker during their duel at the [[Roqoo Depot]].<ref name="Tempest">''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''</ref>

In [[137 ABY]], Imperial Knight [[Elke Vetter]] lost her hand to [[Darth Talon]].<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy 3: Broken, Part 3">[[Legacy (2006) 3|''Legacy'' (2006) 3]]</ref>

Also in 137 ABY, Sith Lord [[Darth Kruhl]] applied ''cho mai'' against [[Rikkar-Du]] in between application of two brutal [[Shiim/Legends|shiim]] marks. He then killed Rikkar-du.<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy 13: Ready to Die">[[Legacy (2006) 13|''Legacy'' (2006) 13]]</ref>

In [[139 ABY]], Imperial Knight [[Jao Assam]] severed both of [[Darth Wredd]]'s hands in the [[Battle of the Floating World]].<ref name="Legacy Volume II">[[Legacy (2013) 18|''Legacy'' (2013) 18]]</ref>
